title: 9 New Movies and Shows to Stream This Weekend on Netflix, JioHotstar, Prime
excerpt: From Parineeti Chopra's investigative thriller 'Reporting Live' to Soori's blockbuster 'Mandaadi', here is what lands on Netflix, JioHotstar, Prime Video and more between October 9 and 11.
body:
• Nine Indian titles drop on streaming between October 9 and 11, led by Parineeti Chopra's investigative thriller 'Reporting Live' and Tamil blockbuster 'Mandaadi' — both on Netflix.
  • Most South Indian titles this week release in four or five dubbed languages, making them easy picks for diaspora households with mixed-language viewers.
  • Reality-TV fans get 'Pati Patni Aur Panga' season 2 on JioHotstar (October 10), hosted by Sonali Bendre and Munawar Faruqui with seven celebrity couples.
  • Best first pick: 'Mandaadi' — a ₹150-crore theatrical blockbuster about traditional boat racing — hits Netflix on October 8.

This weekend's streaming slate is stacked with Indian content. Between October 9 and 11, Netflix, JioHotstar, Prime Video, SonyLIV and regional platforms drop at least nine new Indian movies and shows — from a hard-hitting Hindi investigative thriller to Tamil sports drama, Telugu rom-coms, and celebrity reality TV. Here is the sharp end of the list.

Reporting Live — Netflix, October 9

Parineeti Chopra stars as Sandhya, an ambitious young journalist whose routine investigation pulls her and her veteran cameraman (Deven Bhojani) into the dangerous world of an illegal sand-mining racket. Directed by Dhruv Tripathi and inspired by true events, the Hindi crime thriller co-stars Amol Palekar, Adil Hussain, Shekhar Suman and Nassar — a heavyweight ensemble for a story about the cost of chasing the truth.

Mandaadi — Netflix, October 8

Soori's blockbuster Tamil sports action drama arrives for its OTT premiere. Directed by Mathimaran Pugazhendhi, the film follows former sailboat racer Muthukaali (Soori) and his rival Saattaappuli (Suhas) in the high-energy world of traditional boat racing. It grossed ₹150 crore worldwide on a ₹75 crore budget in theatres — and streams in Tamil, Telugu, Hindi, Malayalam and Kannada.

Epic – First Semester — Netflix, October 9

A Telugu romantic comedy with a London twist. Anand Deverakonda plays Aditya, an aspiring filmmaker who moves to London for his master's degree and ends up flatmates with Kadali (Vaishnavi Chaitanya). Directed by Aditya Haasan, it traces their evolving relationship under the pressure of a nine-month deadline. Also streaming in Hindi, Tamil, Kannada and Malayalam.

Least Eligible Bachelor — Netflix & ETV Win, October 9

Telugu comedy-drama starring Harsha Chemudu and Hyper Aadi, following a young man struggling with societal and familial expectations around marriage. Debuting simultaneously on ETV Win and Netflix, it is built for anyone who has ever sat through an arranged-marriage interrogation — and lived to joke about it.

Pradhama Drishtya Kuttakkar — Netflix, October 9

A Malayalam release joining Netflix's multi-language Friday slate, streaming in Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Hindi. Details are thin, but the five-language launch signals Netflix's confidence — and it is one more option for Malayalam-cinema households.

Pati Patni Aur Panga — Season 2, JioHotstar, October 10

Celebrity couples return for season 2 of the relationship reality show, premiering Saturday and Sunday at 9 PM on Colors TV and streaming on JioHotstar. Hosted by Sonali Bendre and Munawar Faruqui, the confirmed couples include Divyanka Tripathi and Vivek Dahiya, Arjun Bijlani and Neha Swami, Rahul Vaidya and Disha Parmar, and Archana Puran Singh and Parmeet Sethi.

Awarapan 2 — Prime Video, October 9

Emraan Hashmi returns in the sequel to his cult 2007 hit — one for the nostalgia crowd, now streaming on Prime Video.

Khalifa — Simply South / Prime Video, October 9

A South Indian cinema release streaming from October 9 across Simply South, Prime Video, Lionsgate Play and more, in Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Hindi. Note: on Simply South it streams worldwide excluding India.

Paris Cafe — Prime Video, October 9

A Tamil suspense thriller directed by Saraj Seelan, about a daughter's quest to uncover the truth behind her parents' long-hidden separation. Also streaming on Aha Video and Simply South.

How to plan your weekend

Start Friday with 'Reporting Live' for a meaty thriller, or 'Mandaadi' for crowd-pleasing sports drama with the family. 'Epic – First Semester' is the light option. Save 'Pati Patni Aur Panga' for Saturday night reality-TV grazing — and if you are outside India, check whether your region's Netflix carries the multi-language versions before settling in.
